topics.text: Creon of Corinth grants guarded exile after the gifts are exposed and both sons have entered the attendant’s shelter.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-ion
topics.text: Ion names the daily sweeping and water work through which he serves the Delphic temple.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-priestess
topics.text: The priestess tells how she cared for the found child Ion and kept his basket.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-ion
topics.text: Ion reports the failed poisoning, the omen that spared him and the old servant’s exposed part in the plot.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-creusa
topics.text: Creusa tells of her lost child and asks to be heard before judgment in the Delphic account.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-creusa
topics.text: Creusa names her woven cloth, golden snake tokens and olive wreath before the priestess’s basket is presented.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-priestess
topics.text: The priestess entrusts the saved basket and its three signs after Creusa’s own description has been heard.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-creusa
topics.text: Creusa agrees to meet Ion and the priestess at the temple for recognition through the real saved signs.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-creusa
topics.text: Creusa recognises Ion as her son through the basket, woven cloth, golden snakes and olive wreath.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-xuthus
topics.text: Xuthus keeps the public household account of Ion’s place in his family in the earlier Delphic tale.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-creusa
topics.text: Creusa chooses a private recognition with Ion and approves a public excerpt about care and chosen family.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-creusa
topics.text: Creusa authorises her maternal testimony before the temple witnesses and names Apollo as Ion’s father.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-ion
topics.text: Ion chooses to remain with his temple carers while acknowledging Creusa as his mother.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-ion
topics.text: Ion approves the excerpt about the care that kept him alive and the family he and Creusa have chosen.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-creusa
topics.text: Creusa approves the care excerpt honouring Ion’s temple carers and the family they have chosen.

topics.speaker: greek-book-iv-ion-ion
topics.text: Ion approves his lasting temple household and a public excerpt honouring Creusa and his carers.

topics.speaker: greek-aulis-achilles
topics.text: Achilles names the old servant as Agamemnon’s recall carrier and Menelaus as its interceptor.

topics.speaker: greek-aulis-clytemnestra
topics.text: Clytemnestra says the marriage summons concealed the army’s demand for sacrifice.

topics.speaker: greek-aulis-iphigenia
topics.text: Iphigenia gives her own first wish to live and asks Achilles to witness her answer.

topics.speaker: greek-aulis-achilles
topics.text: Achilles repeats the received messenger report of the hind and Calchas’s call for the fleet to sail.

topics.speaker: greek-aulis-clytemnestra
topics.text: Clytemnestra records the living daughter’s refuge at Aulis and the captains’ changed departure.

topics.speaker: greek-aulis-clytemnestra
topics.text: Clytemnestra records her daughter’s death at Aulis and the household grievance carried by the fleet’s voyage.

topics.speaker: greek-aulis-clytemnestra
topics.text: Clytemnestra questions the messenger’s hind report, while Agamemnon confirms Artemis’s rescue and sends her home with the infant as the fleet prepares to sail.

topics.speaker: greek-lemnos-philoctetes
topics.text: Philoctetes entrusts his bow for a short visit to Neoptolemus, with its return agreed.

topics.speaker: greek-lemnos-neoptolemus
topics.text: Neoptolemus names the army’s demand for the man and bow at Troy, and leaves the choice to Philoctetes.

topics.speaker: greek-lemnos-neoptolemus
topics.text: Neoptolemus confesses his deception and accepts that the bow must return before any further agreement.

topics.speaker: greek-lemnos-neoptolemus
topics.text: Neoptolemus reports Heracles’s direction to Troy, his promise of future healing and victory, and his demand for piety.

topics.speaker: greek-lemnos-philoctetes
topics.text: Philoctetes confirms his arrival at Troy with his bow, while his promised healing remains ahead.

topics.speaker: greek-lemnos-philoctetes
topics.text: Philoctetes confirms his chosen homecoming at Trachis with his bow after the journey through Athens and Delphi.

topics.speaker: greek-lemnos-philoctetes
topics.text: Philoctetes confirms his arrival at Troy with his bow under the repaired agreement and its promised care.

topics.speaker: greek-rhesus-hector
topics.text: Hector names the sentry’s current watchword and Dolon’s scouting task before the night raid.

topics.speaker: greek-rhesus-charioteer
topics.text: The wounded charioteer accuses Hector’s men of attacking the Thracian allies after their arrival.

topics.speaker: greek-rhesus-hector
topics.text: Hector attributes the raid to Odysseus and orders care, Rhesus’s burial and a dawn attack on the ships.

topics.speaker: greek-rhesus-hector
topics.text: Hector records Rhesus alive in protected aid duty after the warning and actual withdrawal.

topics.speaker: greek-troy-talthybius
topics.text: Talthybius assigns Andromache to Neoptolemus, Cassandra to Agamemnon and Hecuba to Odysseus in this source account.

topics.speaker: greek-troy-hecuba
topics.text: Hecuba names the captive women’s kin messages and Astyanax’s living care before the later order.

topics.speaker: greek-troy-talthybius
topics.text: Talthybius records the invented earlier rescue terms with a prepared refuge and a consenting crew.

topics.speaker: greek-troy-talthybius
topics.text: Talthybius reports Astyanax’s death and washed body on Hector’s shield after Andromache’s captive departure.

topics.speaker: greek-shipmaster
topics.text: Myrto confirms the two kin-letter carriers’ actual arrival after Andromache’s captive departure and the child’s burial.

topics.speaker: greek-shipmaster
topics.text: Myrto confirms the two kin-letter carriers and Astyanax’s actual refuge under Andromache’s care.

topics.speaker: greek-shipmaster
topics.text: Myrto confirms the family’s actual refuge after the paid reserved voyage left its giver ashore.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-polyxena
topics.text: Polyxena gives her adult farewell and asks Hecuba to remember her dignity in the source sacrifice.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-hecuba
topics.text: Hecuba names Talthybius’s report of Polyxena’s sacrifice and the servant’s discovery of Polydorus at the tide.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-polymestor
topics.text: Polymestor says Priam entrusted Polydorus and gold to his protection before the city fell.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-polymestor
topics.text: Polymestor predicts Hecuba’s changed form and death and Cassandra’s and Agamemnon’s deaths in his source speech.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-hecuba
topics.text: Hecuba reports Agamemnon’s judgment against Polymestor and his order to bury both children before the fleet sails.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-polymestor
topics.text: Polymestor yields the entrusted gold for restitution in the invented hearing while witnesses order both burials.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-hecuba
topics.text: Hecuba names both completed burials after her source revenge and records the king’s predictions as his claims.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-hecuba
topics.text: Hecuba names both completed burials and the actual gold restored through the invented public hearing.

topics.speaker: greek-thrace-hecuba
topics.text: Hecuba names both completed burials and carries the unpaid gold charge while Polymestor retains the wealth.

topics.speaker: greek-susa-atossa
topics.text: Atossa repeats the messenger’s Salamis losses, naming Artembares, Dadaces and Tenagon while Xerxes survives.

topics.speaker: greek-susa-atossa
topics.text: Atossa attributes the warning against further attack and the future defeat at Plataea to Darius’s ghost.

topics.speaker: greek-susa-xerxes
topics.text: Xerxes joins the source-shaped public lament after his actual court arrival while the roll names leaders and ordinary losses.

topics.speaker: greek-susa-atossa
topics.text: Atossa offers the invented private welcome after mother and son reach court and accepts the later full-disclosure duty to families.

topics.speaker: greek-susa-xerxes
topics.text: Xerxes accepts the invented public loss record and appoints household messengers after his actual court arrival.
